newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot natgas extends gains with weather demand.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot natgas extends gains with weather demand.

text.p: U.S. spot natural gas prices gained another five to 10 cents Thursday, propped up early by a rising heating demand in the Midwest and Northeast, industry sources said.
Gulf Coast gas prices moved almost 10 cents higher into the $2.36-2.41 per million British thermal units range, with the higher-priced deals done mostly in early trading.
Temperatures are expected to be more than five degrees Fahrenheit below-normal in the Midwest through Friday and in the Northeast through next week.
As compared to last week, Gulf cash prices are about 40 cents higher.

In the Midcontinent, prices were mostly steady in the high-teens to low-$2.20s as forecasters called for a return to normal temperatures this weekend. These levels are up more than 30 cents from week-ago values.
At the Chicago city-gate, prices also remained stable in the mid-to-high $2.60s.

As temperatures turned cooler on the West Coast and more Canadian gas became available to the U.S. markets, prices at the southern California border eased throughout today's trading. Late deals were reported done in the low-$2.20s, as compared to the $2.30 level seen on Wednesday.

In west Texas, Permian basin prices held fairly strong in the high-teens to low-$2.20s as this gas was now needed in the Midwest and to the east. San Juan prices were discussed in the $2.05-2.10 range.
